author: NASASpaceflight
description:
Boeing says work to correct Starliner’s deficiencies is “going quite well”—but getting the spacecraft back to the International Space Station may depend on more than its hardware. Could Starliner actually return to flight before the end of 2026?

Meanwhile, the spacecraft sent to rescue NASA’s Swift Observatory is itself in trouble after suffering electrical and attitude-control problems. A spent Falcon 9 upper stage is about to crash into the Moon, Amazon wants to deploy more than 5,000 direct-to-device satellites, and NASA’s Artemis III rocket is beginning to take shape.

Also this week: Blue Origin continues repairing Launch Complex 36, RFA One is destacked following a testing issue, Stoke Space reveals flight engines for Nova, NASA fuels the Roman Space Telescope, Europe’s Themis prototype completes a wet dress rehearsal, and ispace selects Japan’s H3 rocket for its next lunar lander.

This is your latest roundup of spaceflight news on This Week in Spaceflight.
